name: Mount Washmore - Base Camp
description: The base of a mountain made entirely of dirty laundry that somehow achieved geological status
long_description: Before you looms Mount Washmore, a geographical impossibility that exists anyway because the universe has a sense of humor. The mountain is composed entirely of dirty laundry - socks, shirts, pants, and unidentifiable garments - all compressed over eons into stratified layers like sedimentary rock. You can literally see different fashion eras preserved in the layers: bell-bottoms from the Disco Period, shoulder pads from the Power Suit Era, and something from the distant past that might be a toga or possibly a very confident bedsheet. The mountain rises into the clouds (which appear to be made of fabric softener vapor), its peak hidden from view. At the base, a small camp has been established by previous expeditions, complete with a tattered flag that reads 'Summit or Bust (Preferably Not Bust).' The air smells like a mixture of gym locker and ancient history. North leads up the mountain trail toward the summit. South leads back to the Bubble Plaza. You can hear distant rumbling from above - either avalanches or the Lint King's legendary snoring, it's hard to tell.

environment.sound: distant rumbling, fabric rustling, and mountain wind
environment.weather: partly cloudy with a chance of sock avalanches
